questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How people adapt to the food of a new country
The history of the British cream tea
How to open a restaurant in Europe
Why Caribbean food is so spicy
questions.why: They explore first impressions of a new culture through its food, hearing from two women.

options: Because it is her favourite meal
Because it is made with frogs
To show that food names in a new country can be surprising
To explain what people usually eat as part of a traditional cream tea
questions.why: She says food can have strange-sounding names, but this dish is made with sausages, not toads.

questions.q: What do we learn about Natalia Tkachenko?
options: She is a Polish chef who moved to Ukraine and then opened a restaurant
She left Ukraine for the Netherlands and later opened a restaurant
She works as a dietitian in Tobago
She owns a restaurant in Ukraine
questions.why: She arrived in the Netherlands from Ukraine, and with Weronika's family opened Natalia's Kitchen.

questions.q: How did Natalia feel when she first arrived?
options: Excited to try new food
Relaxed, because the food was similar
Bored by Dutch cooking
Well outside her comfort zone
questions.why: She says 'at first it felt like I am well out of… my comfort zone'.

questions.q: How did Natalia adapt her cooking?
options: She imported ingredients from Ukraine
She used local ingredients to replace the ones she couldn't find
She stopped cooking Ukrainian food
She learned to cook traditional Dutch recipes and stopped using her own
questions.why: She says some staples weren't available, so she found replacements and cooked with what she had.

questions.q: What shocked Rachel Winter-Roach when she moved to Tobago?
options: The high price of food in the local shops
How little people eat
The hot weather
How food is flavoured and seasoned
questions.why: She says she was 'in for a shock when it came to flavouring and seasoning food'.

questions.q: Why was Caribbean seasoning hard for Rachel to learn?
options: The spices were far too expensive for her to buy in the local shops
Nobody would teach her
Many layers, everyone's own tweaks, and no exact quantities
She didn't like spicy food
questions.why: She says it's 'multiple layers', everyone has their own tweaks, 'and there are no quantities'.

questions.q: What does Rachel suggest about her family while she was learning?
options: They didn't always enjoy her failed attempts
They loved everything she cooked from the very first day
They cooked for her instead
They refused to eat Caribbean food
questions.why: She says her family 'did not always appreciate the errors in the trials'.
